fp10.name: 3D digital twin workflows: packshots, spin video and composite imagery
fp10.scope: Set up Adobe's 3D digital twin starter templates for your client's products (standardized packshots, 360 degree spin video and composite imagery): load each product's USDZ model from local storage, Frame.io or AEM, set the camera angles, render settings and background prompts, run a pilot on a first set of products and confirm the outputs with the creative lead.
fp10.evidence: All 3D Digital Twin workflows are available as starter templates in the Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise home page.

source.title: Adobe Firefly help: Use 3D digital twin workflows

fp10.ext: A USDZ 3D model of each product
fp10.prereq: Your client supplies a USDZ file of each product's 3D model, with geometry, materials and scene data; this service starts from that model and does not create it. Adobe's page says action nodes cannot be added to the standardized packshots and 360 degree spin video workflows unless working with Adobe Field Delivery Engineers, so changes beyond the templates' own settings go through Adobe.
fp10.sow_prereq: The Client provides a USDZ file of each product's 3D model before this service starts. Changes to the packshot and spin video workflows beyond the settings Adobe's templates offer are arranged with Adobe.

prereq_sources.quote: USDZ file containing your 3D product model with geometry, materials, and scene data
Use these workflows when you have a 3D USDZ file of your product and need to generate consistent marketing content across multiple angles, environments, or formats.
select Upload and choose your USDZ file from local storage, Frame.io, or AEM
Users cannot add additional Action nodes unless working with Adobe Field Delivery Engineers.

fp10_note: Rechecked today on helpx.adobe.com. The help page Use 3D digital twin workflows (last updated Apr 20, 2026) documents the three starter templates (Standardized Packshots, 360 degree Spin Video, Composite Imagery) with step-by-step use and carries no beta, preview or coming label; the only uses of the word preview on it are the ordinary ones (a 3D preview, the Preview button). The Operations page lists the same three workflows with no label, and the Creative Production home page lists the Product Assets templates built on digital twins. One service written, optional. It needs a USDZ model of each product: Adobe's Operations page also lists Digital Twin Authoring as Adobe's own work charged in Operations, so the service starts from an existing model and does not create one. Adobe's footnote (action nodes cannot be added without Adobe Field Delivery Engineers) is marked on Standardized packshots (2D and 3D) and 360 degree spin video, not on Composite imagery (3D); the prerequisite says so. ext is filled with the USDZ model, which is a file and not an Adobe license, so drop ext and keep prereq if ext is reserved for products. prereq, sow_prereq and prereq_sources are extra fields beyond the FP01 to FP09 format. Overlap: FP03 covers Adobe's banner and product asset templates in general; FP10 is only the three 3D templates and their USDZ input. Not covered here: what Adobe announced at MAX on Nov 10 2026 for 3D Digital Twin (changing a product's labels and materials) is not on these pages and is left out as a coming feature. The first fetch with a browser-style User-Agent was refused by helpx (Access Denied); the pages were read with plain curl, the way verify_quotes.py fetches them.

ideation.note: Documented on Experience League since Nov 9 2026, six pages found through the English sitemap, at setup level (access levels, licenses, permissions, briefs, export to Planning records). Every article page opens with Adobe's banner that the functionality is not yet generally available and is available only as part of the Ideation space Beta program; Adobe gives a closed beta, an open beta targeted for November 12, 2026 and general availability targeted for February 1, 2027. Under Adam's rule on beta features no service is written; WP09 stays free. When the label goes, it belongs to Workfront Planning as WP09, with these conditions Adobe states today: a Workfront Workflow package with a Workfront Planning package (not Planning as a standalone product during the beta), CX Enterprise Coworker in Workfront turned on, AWS only (Azure and GCP are not supported), and Coworker is not currently available to health care, finance and some other industries, so Ideation space is not available to them either. Adobe's own spelling varies on the page (Adobe Enterprise CX Coworker, Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker).
